clue.text: One of two books US male adapted

definitions.note: the Old Testament has First and Second Samuel, two books under one name

indicators.note: something adapted is altered to a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American man's story gets turned into a screen adaptation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible holds two books named after the prophet, 1 and 2 Samuel.

clue.text: Jelly made from seaweed or a fish

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted freshwater fish, also called garfish

explanation.surface: A cook wonders whether a jelly comes from seaweed or from a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like it offers two definitions, but it is only a link; 'a fish' is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is the gelatinous substance extracted from red algae, used to set desserts and culture media.

clue.text: Opens zip in front of underwear (10 wearing new smalls)

indicators.note: zip is placed in among the other letters, inside the run they build
the front of a word is its opening letter, here of underwear
the smalls are worn by the number, so they go round it

parts.note: smalls, British slang for underwear, gives two small letters, S and S
the number ten written as a word
zip means nothing; FA is short for 'Sweet FA', British slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: Someone opens a zip on fresh underwear, perhaps ten new pairs of smalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' wraps the smalls round the number, and 'in' slips zip into the resulting run. Smalls is British slang for underwear; Sweet FA is slang for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To open a fastened thing is to undo its clasp, button or zip.

clue.text: Watch as diver is stopped by knockout

indicators.note: the diver is plugged in the middle by the knockout, which sits inside it

parts.note: a loon is the North American name for the diving bird Britons call a diver
KO is the standard abbreviation for a knockout in boxing

explanation.surface: Spectators watch as a diver is felled by a knockout blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diver' looks like a person in the water, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To look on is to be a spectator, watching without taking part.

clue.text: Polite and restrained doctor: our odd epithet suggests Dr Crippen, principally

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged
principally points to the principal, leading letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A well-mannered doctor's odd nickname evokes the notorious Dr Crippen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun naming Crippen's trade, but it is the verb signalling the anagram of OUR plus OESDC. Crippen was a doctor hanged in 1910 for murdering his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorous behaviour is proper and seemly, in keeping with good taste.

clue.text: Fellow can sleep around with lead actor

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

indicators.note: the letters are scattered around into a new order

explanation.surface: A man can sleep about with the star of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like the star role, but it joins the anagram fodder that 'around' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Pleasence was an English screen performer, famous as Blofeld and as Dr Loomis in Halloween.

clue.text: Queen maybe taking online bloody class!

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, and 'maybe' marks it as an example
E as in e-mail, the prefix for electronic or online
gory means covered in blood

explanation.surface: The Queen joins in with an internet lesson that turns violent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' looks royal, but it is the cat sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A category is a group of things sharing a characteristic, a division or type.

clue.text: First stripper's top having been shed excites debauched old men?

indicators.note: of the two matching letters in the verb, the one nearer the start is dropped
shedding a piece means losing it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: rouses means stirs up or excites

indicators.note: the top of a word is its opening letter, here of stripper's

explanation.surface: A stripper takes off her top, arousing lecherous old men.
explanation.walkthrough: The first S of ROUSES is dropped, not the second; 'First' says which.
explanation.definitionFit: A roué is a dissolute, pleasure-seeking man, often older; the question mark admits not every one is old.

clue.text: Aunt's plane's taken off for Nice? On the contrary

indicators.note: a plane taking off also suggests the letters launched into a new order

explanation.surface: An aunt's plane has departed for the French city of Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'plane' stands for 'has', a link. 'Nice' looks like the Riviera city, but the definition is the opposite of nice.
explanation.definitionFit: Disagreeable or nasty is the reverse of pleasant or agreeable.

clue.text: Drink with doctor about to show some a cheeky side?

definitions.text: to show some a cheeky side?
definitions.note: to moon is to bare one's buttocks, so a half one shows a single cheek

parts.note: a half is a half pint of beer
MO is Medical Officer, a military doctor
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A drinker with a doctor reveals a cheeky streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheeky' looks like impudent, but means buttocks: mooning is baring your backside, so a half version shows one cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful idea: a partial mooning, exposing just one buttock rather than the whole rear.

clue.text: Outdoes frequent fake news tweeter? Success at last!

parts.note: Donald Trump, who often tweeted about 'fake news'

indicators.note: at last points to the closing letter of the word Success

explanation.surface: A habitual tweeter crying fake news finally succeeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To trump is to beat or surpass, as a trump card beats other suits.

clue.text: Golly! So stern, after beating a politician like Trump?

indicators.note: beaten things are battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone stern after a thrashing of a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A snollygoster is old US slang for a shrewd, unprincipled politician.

clue.text: A sticker getting top to bottom covered by 'Must see you later in Spain'

indicators.note: the inner letters are covered on both sides by the outer word

parts.note: has to means must

indicators.note: in a down entry the top letter goes to the bottom, moving from first to last

parts.note: glue is a sticker, something that sticks

explanation.surface: A sticker on a sign telling you to bid farewell in Spanish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting top to bottom' turns GLUE into LUEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasta luego is the Spanish farewell meaning until later.

clue.text: Content to catch a real murderer? You'll need to run fast!

definitions.meaning: William Hare of Burke and Hare killed people in 1820s Edinburgh to sell corpses
an animal famous for its speed, which you would need to sprint to catch

indicators.note: the content of a phrase is what it holds, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: A detective is happy to nab a genuine killer, but warns of a chase.
explanation.walkthrough: Burke and Hare were notorious Edinburgh murderers who sold bodies to anatomists.
explanation.definitionFit: Hares are swift long-eared mammals; Hare was also one of the infamous body-snatching killers.

clue.text: Short small red salad ingredient dipped in pea soup? Heaven!

indicators.note: the shortened vegetable goes into the soup
soup is a mixture, so the letters are mixed
short means cut off before the end, losing the last letter

parts.note: a radish is a small red root eaten in salads

explanation.surface: A shortened radish dunked into pea soup is bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soup' mixes the pea, 'Short' docks the salad vegetable's last letter, and 'dipped in' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a synonym for heaven, a place of perfect bliss.

clue.text: Outlaw carrying weapon, not a dead duck

indicators.note: dead carries the shortened weapon inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not a means the letter a is dropped

parts.note: a spear is a weapon
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so O

explanation.surface: An outlaw armed but unable to shoot even a dead duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' strips a letter from the weapon, which 'carrying' tucks into dead. In cricket a duck is a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless criminal, especially in the Wild West.

clue.text: Warning one doctor that's accepted back in National Front supporter?

indicators.note: the warning, one and doctor take in another letter among them

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout
I is the Roman numeral one
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

indicators.note: the back of a word is its closing letter, here of National

explanation.surface: A cautionary note about a doctor backing the far-right National Front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National Front' looks like the British far-right party, but splits: National gives L, 'Front supporter' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A front leg or arm supports an animal's front end.

clue.text: Nothing to get by describing beginner on stringed instrument

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round, so these letters go round the other

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
cope means manage or get by

indicators.note: the beginner on a word is its opening letter, here of stringed

explanation.surface: A novice gets nowhere coping with a stringed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stringed instrument' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: An otoscope is the device doctors use to look into ears.

clue.text: Function held in premises in Epsom

indicators.note: held in means the letters are contained in these words

explanation.surface: An event takes place on premises in Epsom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' looks like a party, but it is a trigonometric function. Epsom is an English town known for its racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine is a trigonometric ratio, a mathematical function of an angle.

clue.text: Suspect plot is one created by Shakespeare

indicators.note: suspect means dubious, not straight, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dodgy plot by Shakespeare is under suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistol is a swaggering character in Henry IV Part 2, Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor.

clue.text: Trump finally replaced by Biden, at first perhaps he talks tripe?

definitions.text: Trump finally replaced by Biden, at first perhaps he talks tripe?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise
one letter is swapped out and another put in its place
finally points to the closing letter of Trump
at first points to the opening letter of Biden

explanation.surface: A dig at Trump, now replaced by Biden, as a talker of nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced by' swaps the P of TRIPE for B, giving HE TALKS TRIBE, which 'perhaps' rearranges. The whole clue doubles as the definition, aimed at Trump.
explanation.definitionFit: A blatherskite is a person who talks voluble nonsense, a garrulous babbler.

clue.text: For group of criminals, regular choice of store is Aldi

indicators.note: a regular choice takes every other letter of these words

explanation.surface: Crooks routinely choose Aldi as their supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldi is a discount supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A triad is a Chinese organised crime syndicate.

clue.text: Fairy Queen penned by Greek character

indicators.note: the queen is shut in by the Greek letter, as in a pen

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A fairy queen is written about by a Greek author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a figure in a story, but it is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A peri is a fairy or elf in Persian mythology.

clue.text: Sign garage needs vacating by small car

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: the Mini is a classic small British car

explanation.surface: A garage sign says small cars must clear out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' looks like a notice, but it is a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the twins, is a zodiac sign.

clue.text: Fertilisers Charlie values

parts.note: a charlie is British slang for a fool, as is a nit
rates means values or assesses

explanation.surface: A gardener called Charlie rates fertilisers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like a name, but is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrates are nitrogen salts widely used to fertilise soil.

clue.text: Could be bent double agent? Not the chap Blofeld shot

indicators.note: shot means ruined, wrecked, so the letters are rearranged
not means without, so the chap's letters come out of the word

parts.note: a gent is a chap, a gentleman

explanation.surface: A double agent, not the man shot by the Bond villain Blofeld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not the chap' turns AGENT into A; 'shot' scrambles A with BLOFELD. Blofeld is James Bond's arch-enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foldable can be creased over on itself, doubled over.

clue.text: Convenience store primarily secures money with one cash handling company

indicators.note: secures means holds firmly, so these letters are taken in

parts.note: a convenience is a public toilet, a loo

indicators.note: primarily points to the opening letter of store

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for money, as in economics
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A convenience store keeps cash secure with a security firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convenience store' reads as one phrase, but splits: convenience is the British term for a public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Loomis is an international firm that transports and processes banknotes.
